postTitle: The 1-line trick to skip expensive recalculations in React: useMemo
postContent:
Hook: React apps feel fast when heavy work isn’t repeated.
This is where useMemo shines. It caches a value and reuses it on subsequent renders.
It only recomputes when its dependencies change.
Use it for expensive calculations or heavy filtering.

In plain terms: you provide a function that returns the derived value and a dependencies array.
If dependencies stay the same, React returns the cached value instead of recomputing.
Remember: useMemo helps only when the calculation is expensive; otherwise the overhead isn’t worth it.

tehnicalChallange.title: Memoize an extra derived value (completed count)
tehnicalChallange.description: Add a second memoized value that counts completed todos. Use useMemo and display the count alongside the list. Ensure it recalculates only when todos or tab change.
